title: Microscale Vortex-assisted Electroporator for Sequential Molecular Delivery
protocol: Plate 1×105 cells/ml of metastatic breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 in a volume of 10 ml per tissue culture T75 flask in Leibovitz’s L-15 Medium supplemented with 10% (v/v) fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Incubate MDA-MB-231 cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 0% CO2 environment for 2 days.
Treat cells with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA for 2 min to harvest cells.
Add 8 ml of the growth media to inactivate trypsin’s enzymatic activity.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 200 × g to pellet cells.
Resuspend cells in Dulbecco’s phosphate buffered saline (DPBS, 1x, without Ca2+ and Mg2+) to a final concentration of 5 × 105 cells/ml.
Design a microfluidic device with AutoCAD as illustrated in Figure 1.
Create an inlet with multiple injection ports on the device.
Include coarse filters within the design.
Construct two parallel straight rectangular inertial focusing channels, each measuring L = 7 mm, W = 40 μm, and H = 70 μm.
Place 5 electroporation chambers in each individual straight channel, spaced 800 μm apart with a width of WC = 400 μm.
Insert two via holes for aluminum electrodes in the design.
Position two transversally adjacent electroporation chambers to share the hole for the negative electrode.
Merge the two straight channels into an outlet at the downstream end of the electroporation region.
Convert the CAD file with micro-patterns to a GDSII file using LinkCAD.
Write micro-patterns on a 5” x 5” photomask blank using a laser mask writer.
Follow the manufacturer’s protocol to develop the mask, including photoresist developing and chrome etching.
Remove the resist according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Alternatively, purchase high-resolution transparency with micro-patterns (>20,000 dpi) from a third-party manufacturer for use as a photomask.
Ensure final microscale features on the photomask are transparent to match the polarity of negative photoresist.
Use standard soft lithography techniques to fabricate the casting mold of the device design.
Spin coat a negative photoresist on a 4 inch silicon wafer at 2,000 rpm to achieve a thickness of 70 μm.
Prebake the wafer with negative photoresist for 20 min at 95 °C.
Contact the mask with the wafer.
Expose the wafer to a UV source at 17.4 mJ/cm² for 80 sec using a mask aligner.
Develop the exposed wafer in a SU-8 developer for 4 min.
Measure the thickness of the developed photoresist using a surface profilometer.
Mix a 10:1 ratio of elastomer to curing agent (silicone elastomer kit).
Pour the mixture onto the casting mold to generate PDMS replicas.
Degas the casting elastomer for 30 min.
Cure the casting mold with degassed elastomer in an oven at 70 °C for 2 hr.
Delaminate cured PDMS replica with microchannel patterns from the mold.
Punch holes for inlets, outlet, and electrode insertions using a pin vise with a cutting edge diameter of 0.76 mm.
Treat a glass slide in an oxygen-plasma cleaner for 7 sec at 75 W radio frequency power and 500 mTorr oxygen partial pressure.
Bond PDMS replicas to the treated glass slide to create enclosed microfluidic channels.
Insert aluminum electrodes (0.029” OD) into designated places via holes in the microchannel.
Insert an outlet PEEK tubing (1/32” OD) into designated places via holes in the microchannel.
Connect electrical equipment responsible for generating high-voltage short square-wave pulses to aluminum electrodes in contact with flowing solutions in the PDMS mold.
Prepare four 50 ml centrifuge tubes containing DPBS, and attach each tube to its respective vial holder connected to the pneumatic flow control system.
Attach inlet PEEK tubing from the vial holders into the respective inlet holes in the microfluidic device.
Set the magnitude of square-wave pulses to 100 V for an electric field strength across the electroporation chamber equivalent to 0.7 kV/cm.
Set the pressure regulator to 40 psi to uniformly pressurize all sample vials using a manually adjustable nitrogen source.
Utilize a high-speed manifold activated by custom-built LabVIEW software to timely activate individual solution ports.
Open the custom-built LabVIEW software labeled Valve Runner, and click run from the dropdown menu entitled operate.
Click on each corresponding valve icon to turn on valves.
Activate the DPBS reservoir (i.e., washing solution) valve for 1.5 min to prime flow speed.
Switch the active solution port from the washing solution to the cell solution to trap cells in the electroporation chamber for 30 sec.
Flow both washing and cell solutions through the device simultaneously for 10 sec before switching ports.
Turn on the washing port and flush the device for 20 sec to remove non-trapped contaminating cells.
Inject the solution containing the first molecule of interest (0.2 mg/ml of 3,000 Da neutral and anionic dextran molecules or 1.5 mg/ml of 70,000 Da neutral dextran molecule) into the device.
Apply five short pulses (Δt= 30 msec with 2 sec intervals) promptly after injection and monitor electrical pulses using an oscilloscope.
Incubate cells for 100 s in the molecular solution.
Flush the device with the washing solution for 100 s to remove excess molecules.
Release the cells in a 96-well plate for downstream analysis by lowering the operating pressure below 5 psi.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate containing processed cells for 5 min at 228 × g.
Remove the supernatant that contains excess fluorescent molecules.
Resuspend cells in DPBS for flow cytometry analysis.
Load cells in the flow cytometer for molecular uptake efficiency analysis.
